proposals.before: Shao Xu feared an attack by Shi Le and first begged help from Duan Pidi; Pidi sent his younger brother Duan Wenying to relieve Shao Xu.
proposals.after: Shao Xu feared an attack by Shi Le and first begged help from Duan Pidi; Pidi sent his younger brother Duan Wenyang to relieve Shao Xu.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Fearing Shi Le's assault, he appealed first to Duan Pidi, who sent his brother Wenying to his rescue.
proposals.after: Fearing Shi Le's assault, he appealed first to Duan Pidi, who sent his brother Wenyang to his rescue.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Before Wenying had arrived, Shi Le had already led eight thousand horsemen to besiege Shao Xu.
proposals.after: Before Wenyang had arrived, Shi Le had already led eight thousand horsemen to besiege Shao Xu.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shi Le had always feared the Xianbei, and when he heard Wenying was coming he abandoned his siege equipment and fled east.
proposals.after: Shi Le had always feared the Xianbei, and when he heard Wenyang was coming he abandoned his siege equipment and fled east.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shi Le had always dreaded the Xianbei; at word of Wenying's approach he abandoned his engines and bolted east.
proposals.after: Shi Le had always dreaded the Xianbei; at word of Wenyang's approach he abandoned his engines and bolted east.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shao Xu and Wenying pursued Shi Le to Anling but did not overtake him; they captured Shi Le's appointed officials, drove off more than three thousand households, also sent cavalry to raid Shi Le's northern border, plundered Changshan, and likewise returned with two thousand households.
proposals.after: Shao Xu and Wenyang pursued Shi Le to Anling but did not overtake him; they captured Shi Le's appointed officials, drove off more than three thousand households, also sent cavalry to raid Shi Le's northern border, plundered Changshan, and likewise returned with two thousand households.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shao Xu and Wenying chased him to Anling but could not catch him; they took the officials Shi Le had installed, marched off over three thousand families, sent riders to scour his northern marches and sack Changshan, and came back with two thousand more households besides.
proposals.after: Shao Xu and Wenyang chased him to Anling but could not catch him; they took the officials Shi Le had installed, marched off over three thousand families, sent riders to scour his northern marches and sack Changshan, and came back with two thousand more households besides.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shao Xu sent his nephew Cun, interior governor of Wuyi, and Wenying to lead Pidi's followers to forage in Pingyuan; they were defeated by Shi Jilong.
proposals.after: Shao Xu sent his nephew Cun, interior governor of Wuyi, and Wenyang to lead Pidi's followers to forage in Pingyuan; they were defeated by Shi Jilong.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: He dispatched his nephew Cun, Wuyi's interior governor, with Wenying to escort Pidi's people into Pingyuan for supplies; Shi Hu shattered their force.
proposals.after: He dispatched his nephew Cun, Wuyi's interior governor, with Wenyang to escort Pidi's people into Pingyuan for supplies; Shi Hu shattered their force.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Taixing, Shao Xu sent Cun and Wenying to garrison the Yellow Turban fort at Jinan in order to pressure Cao Yi; Yi feared and sued for peace.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Taixing, Shao Xu sent Cun and Wenyang to garrison the Yellow Turban fort at Jinan in order to pressure Cao Yi; Yi feared and sued for peace.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Early in the Taixing era he sent Cun and Wenying to hold the old Yellow Turban stronghold at Jinan and squeeze Cao Yi until Yi sued for peace.
proposals.after: Early in the Taixing era he sent Cun and Wenyang to hold the old Yellow Turban stronghold at Jinan and squeeze Cao Yi until Yi sued for peace.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: After a long time Pidi and his younger brother Wenying with Zhu, Ji, and the others were all captured; only Cun broke out of the encirclement and fled south, but on the road was killed by bandits.
proposals.after: After a long time Pidi and his younger brother Wenyang with Zhu, Ji, and the others were all captured; only Cun broke out of the encirclement and fled south, but on the road was killed by bandits.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: In time Pidi, Wenying, Zhu, and Ji were all taken; only Cun burst the ring and ran south, only to die at bandit hands on the road.
proposals.after: In time Pidi, Wenyang, Zhu, and Ji were all taken; only Cun burst the ring and ran south, only to die at bandit hands on the road.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: At that time Guo Mo, whom Liu Kun had provisionally appointed prefect of Henan, was pressed by Liu Yuan and begged to return to Li Ju; Li Ju was about to have his nephew Guo Song go welcome him but did not dare advance.
proposals.after: At that time Guo Mo, whom Liu Kun had provisionally appointed prefect of Henei, was pressed by Liu Yuan and begged to return to Li Ju; Li Ju was about to have his nephew Guo Song go welcome him but did not dare advance.
proposals.reason: The source office is 河內太守, Prefect of Henei, not Henan.

proposals.before: Guo Mo, Liu Kun's acting prefect of Henan, was harried by Liu Yuan and begged Li Ju for refuge; Li Ju meant to send his nephew Guo Song to escort him in, but Song hesitated to move.
proposals.after: Guo Mo, Liu Kun's acting prefect of Henei, was harried by Liu Yuan and begged Li Ju for refuge; Li Ju meant to send his nephew Guo Song to escort him in, but Song hesitated to move.
proposals.reason: The source office is 河內太守, Prefect of Henei, not Henan.

proposals.before: The Tuge of old feared the Xianbei; they therefore intercepted Zhang Zhao to request his support as a diversion, and Zhao consented.
proposals.after: The Tuge had long feared the Xianbei; Li Ju therefore invited Zhang Zhao to lend visible support, and Zhao consented.
proposals.reason: 屠各 are the feared enemy, not the party inviting 張肇; the following 賊望見鮮卑不戰而走 confirms that Li Ju uses Zhang Zhao's Xianbei as support.

proposals.before: The Tuge had always dreaded Xianbei horse, so they waylaid Zhang Zhao and begged him to show a banner of support; Zhao agreed.
proposals.after: The Tuge had always dreaded Xianbei horse, so Li Ju asked Zhang Zhao to lend their visible support; Zhao agreed.
proposals.reason: 屠各 are the feared enemy, not the party inviting 張肇; the next unit says the enemy fled on seeing the Xianbei.

proposals.before: Li Ju thereupon memorialized recommending Guo Song as General Who Rouses Might and magistrate of Yangzhai, dammed the water and built ramparts, simultaneously farming and defending, as a plan to destroy the bandits.
proposals.after: Li Ju thereupon memorialized recommending Guo Song as General Who Rouses Might and magistrate of Yangzhai; relying on the water, Guo Song built ramparts, simultaneously farming and defending, as a plan to destroy the bandits.
proposals.reason: 阻水 means to use the water as a defensive barrier, not to dam it; the continuing subject is 郭誦.

proposals.before: He then recommended Guo Song for General Who Rouses Might and magistrate of Yangzhai, had him throw up dikes and forts along the water, plow and hold the line, and starve the enemy out.
proposals.after: He then recommended Guo Song for General Who Rouses Might and magistrate of Yangzhai; Guo Song relied on the water, built ramparts, and combined farming with defense as a plan to destroy the enemy.
proposals.reason: 阻水築壘 says Guo Song relied on the water and built ramparts; it does not say he built dikes or planned to starve the enemy.

proposals.before: Guo Song took five hundred of his best fighters, ran Shi Sheng down at the old Panczhi post station, and thrashed him again.
proposals.after: Guo Song took five hundred of his best fighters, ran Shi Sheng down at the old Panzhi post station, and thrashed him again.
proposals.reason: 磐脂 is rendered Panzhi in the literal field; “Panczhi” is a typographical name error.

proposals.before: The welcoming of Guo Mo was entirely because of you; facing peril you fled away—you are sure to have left him in the lurch."
proposals.after: Our receiving Guo Mo was entirely because of you. Now that he has fled in the face of danger, you must detain him."
proposals.reason: 郭默 is the one who 臨難逃走; 李矩 is ordering 郭誦 to pursue and retain him (其必留之), not accusing Guo Song of fleeing.

proposals.before: You alone talked me into sheltering Guo Mo; when danger came you bolted and abandoned him."
proposals.after: You alone talked me into sheltering Guo Mo; now he has fled when danger came, and you must detain him."
proposals.reason: 郭默 is the fugitive and 郭誦 is the addressee ordered to stop him; the current version reverses the attribution and omits the order.

proposals.before: When Liu Yao pressed Luoyang, Wang Jun sent supervisor Wang Chang and others to lead Jilujuan and his younger brother Wenying and cousin Mobo to attack Shi Le at Xiangguo.
proposals.after: When Liu Yao pressed Luoyang, Wang Jun sent supervisor Wang Chang and others to lead Jilujuan and his younger brother Wenyang and cousin Mobo to attack Shi Le at Xiangguo.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: As Liu Yao closed on Luoyang, Wang Jun dispatched Wang Chang to lead Jilujuan, Wenying, and Mobo against Shi Le at Xiangguo.
proposals.after: As Liu Yao closed on Luoyang, Wang Jun dispatched Wang Chang to lead Jilujuan, Wenyang, and Mobo against Shi Le at Xiangguo.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Le held Mobo hostage and sent an envoy to sue for peace with Jilujuan; Jilujuan was about to consent when Wenying remonstrated: "We received orders to punish Shi Le—would you for Mobo alone release a foe already in the bag?
proposals.after: Le held Mobo hostage and sent an envoy to sue for peace with Jilujuan; Jilujuan was about to consent when Wenyang remonstrated: "We received orders to punish Shi Le—would you for Mobo alone release a foe already in the bag?
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shi Le held Mobo hostage and sued for peace; Jilujuan was ready to agree when Wenying objected: "We were ordered to crush Shi Le—would you loose a cornered prey for one man?
proposals.after: Shi Le held Mobo hostage and sued for peace; Jilujuan was ready to agree when Wenyang objected: "We were ordered to crush Shi Le—would you loose a cornered prey for one man?
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Jilujuan ordered Wenying to ally with Shi Jilong by oath as brothers, then led the horsemen back.
proposals.after: Jilujuan ordered Wenyang to ally with Shi Jilong by oath as brothers, then led the horsemen back.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Jilujuan had Wenying swear brotherhood with Shi Hu and then marched his cavalry home.
proposals.after: Jilujuan had Wenyang swear brotherhood with Shi Hu and then marched his cavalry home.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Yet Mobo both wished to repay an old kindness and, moreover, because Pidi was abroad, wished to surprise-seize his state; he therefore slandered Pidi to Shefuchen and Jilujuan, saying: "To follow sons and younger brothers on account of fathers and elder brothers?
proposals.after: Yet Mobo both wished to repay an old kindness and, moreover, because Pidi was abroad, wished to seize his state by surprise; he therefore slandered Pidi to Shefuchen and Jilujuan, saying: "Should fathers and elder brothers follow sons and younger brothers?
proposals.reason: 父兄 and 子弟 are fathers/elder brothers and sons/younger brothers; the current question reverses the syntax.

proposals.before: Mobo meant both to repay an old debt and, with Pidi away, to seize his domain; he whispered to Shefuchen and Jilujuan, "Why should fathers and uncles take orders from sons and nephews?
proposals.after: Mobo meant both to repay an old debt and, with Pidi away, to seize his domain; he whispered to Shefuchen and Jilujuan, "Why should fathers and elder brothers take orders from sons and younger brothers?
proposals.reason: 父兄/子弟 does not say uncles/nephews; it contrasts senior and junior generations or siblings.

proposals.before: He also ordered Wenying north to punish Mobo's younger brother at Ji city; when returning, eighty li from the city, hearing Xu had already been lost, the host feared and scattered, and again was intercepted by Shi Jilong; Wenying with several hundred of his personal guard fought bitterly, broke them, and only then was able to enter the city.
proposals.after: He also ordered Wenyang north to punish Mobo's younger brother at Ji city; when returning, eighty li from the city, hearing Xu had already been lost, the host feared and scattered, and again was intercepted by Shi Jilong; Wenyang with several hundred of his personal guard fought bitterly, broke them, and only then was able to enter the city.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: He sent Wenying north against Mobo's brother at Ji; on the way back, eighty li from the walls, word came that Shao Xu had fallen—the army panicked and broke. Shi Hu barred the road, but Wenying cut through with a few hundred household guards and fought his way inside.
proposals.after: He sent Wenyang north against Mobo's brother at Ji; on the way back, eighty li from the walls, word came that Shao Xu had fallen—the army panicked and broke. Shi Hu barred the road, but Wenyang cut through with a few hundred household guards and fought his way inside.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shi Jilong again raided beneath the walls; Wenying ascended the walls and looked down, wishing to go out and strike them, but Pidi did not permit it.
proposals.after: Shi Jilong again raided beneath the walls; Wenyang ascended the walls and looked down, wishing to go out and strike them, but Pidi did not permit it.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shi Hu raided the suburbs again; Wenying mounted the wall, itching to sortie, but Pidi forbade it.
proposals.after: Shi Hu raided the suburbs again; Wenyang mounted the wall, itching to sortie, but Pidi forbade it.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Wenying said: "I am famed for courage; therefore the common people lean on me.
proposals.after: Wenyang said: "I am famed for courage; therefore the common people lean on me.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Wenying said, "My name is courage—the people lean on me for that.
proposals.after: Wenyang said, "My name is courage—the people lean on me for that.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: His horse grew exhausted and fell; he could not rise.
proposals.after: His horse grew exhausted, collapsed, and could not rise.
proposals.reason: In 馬乏，伏不能起, the exhausted horse is the subject that collapses and cannot rise; the current field wrongly makes Wenyang unable to rise.

proposals.before: His mount gave out and threw him; he could not remount.
proposals.after: His mount gave out, collapsed, and could not rise.
proposals.reason: 伏不能起 describes the horse lying down unable to rise; “threw him” and “could not remount” are not in the source.

proposals.before: Wenying cursed him: "You have acted the bandit tyrant and long ago deserved death; my elder brother did not use my plan, therefore he let you reach this point; I would rather die than be captured by you."
proposals.after: Wenyang cursed him: "You have acted the bandit tyrant and long ago deserved death; my elder brother did not use my plan, therefore he let you reach this point; I would rather die than be captured by you."
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Wenying snarled back, "You have ravaged like a wolf and earned death a hundred times; my brother spurned my counsel and let you come this far—I will die before I let you take me."
proposals.after: Wenyang snarled back, "You have ravaged like a wolf and earned death a hundred times; my brother spurned my counsel and let you come this far—I will die before I let you take me."
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Shi Jilong's army on four sides loosened horse nets and leather screens to shield themselves and advanced to seize Wenying.
proposals.after: Shi Jilong's army on four sides loosened horse nets and leather screens to shield themselves and advanced to seize Wenyang.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Wenying fought from the chen hour to the shen hour; only when his strength was exhausted was he at last captured.
proposals.after: Wenyang fought from the chen hour to the shen hour; only when his strength was exhausted was he at last captured.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Today affairs press me; I wished to return blame to the court, yet I am pressed and blocked; my loyal sincerity cannot be achieved.
proposals.after: Today affairs press me; I wished to return to the court to answer for my guilt, yet I am pressed and blocked; my loyal sincerity cannot be fulfilled.
proposals.reason: 歸罪朝廷 means return to court to submit/answer for one's guilt, not shift blame onto the court.

proposals.before: Wenying likewise met death by poisoned wine; only Mobo survived.
proposals.after: Wenyang likewise met death by poisoned wine; only Mobo survived.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Wenying too was poisoned; only Mobo was left alive.
proposals.after: Wenyang too was poisoned; only Mobo was left alive.
proposals.reason: 文鴦 is Wenyang (鴦, yang), not Wenying.

proposals.before: Wei Jun came from Dong'e in the eastern commandery but had settled in Guanzhong.
proposals.after: Wei Jun came from Dong'e in Dong Commandery but had settled in Guanzhong.
proposals.reason: 東郡 is the proper name Dong Commandery, not a generic “eastern commandery.”

proposals.before: At that time the capital district was desolate and straitened; Jun by plunder obtained grain and wheat, presented them to Emperor Huai, and the emperor appointed him General Who Rouses Might and prefect of Pingyang, his commissary post remaining as before.
proposals.after: At that time the capital district was desolate and straitened; Jun by plunder obtained grain and wheat, presented them to Emperor Huai, and the emperor appointed him General Who Displays Might and prefect of Pingyang, his commissary post remaining as before.
proposals.reason: 揚威將軍 is General Who Displays Might; “Rouses Might” confuses the title with 揚武.

proposals.before: The capital was starving; Wei Jun seized grain and sent it to Emperor Huai, who named him General Who Rouses Might and prefect of Pingyang while keeping him on supply duty.
proposals.after: The capital was starving; Wei Jun seized grain and sent it to Emperor Huai, who named him General Who Displays Might and prefect of Pingyang while keeping him on supply duty.
proposals.reason: 揚威將軍 is General Who Displays Might; “Rouses Might” confuses the title with 揚武.

proposals.before: After Luoyang fell he built a fort on the stone bridge north of the river, gathered survivors, and slowly rebuilt an arsenal.
proposals.after: After Luoyang fell he garrisoned Shiliang Fort north of the Luo, supported the survivors, and gradually repaired military equipment.
proposals.reason: 屯於洛北石梁塢 says he garrisoned the named Shiliang Fort north of the Luo; it does not say he built a fort on a stone bridge.

proposals.before: When Liu Yao attacked Luoyang, he followed Jun to answer the crisis, first leading troops to defend the Metal Moat fort, therefore there was nothing else amiss.
proposals.after: When Liu Yao attacked Luoyang, he followed Jun to answer the crisis, first leading troops to defend the Metal Moat fort, and therefore escaped harm.
proposals.reason: 故得無他 means that he consequently came to no harm, not that “there was nothing else amiss.”

proposals.before: During Liu Yao's siege of Luoyang he rode with Wei Jun to the rescue and held the Metal Moat first, so the line held.
proposals.after: During Liu Yao's siege of Luoyang he rode with Wei Jun to the rescue and held the Metal Moat first, thereby escaping harm.
proposals.reason: 故得無他 states the consequence for Wei Gai; it does not say that a military line held.

proposals.before: He withdrew to Xinye, marched with Zhou Fang to crush Du Zeng, and was enfeoffed prefect of Shunyang.
proposals.after: He withdrew to Xinye, marched with Zhou Fang to crush Du Zeng, and was appointed prefect of Shunyang.
proposals.reason: 詔以該為順陽太守 is an appointment to office, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: When Wang Dun rose, Gan Zhuo of Liang province stayed neutral and sounded Wei Gai with a forged order from Dun.
proposals.after: When Wang Dun rose, Gan Zhuo of Liang province did not join him and, wishing to test Wei Gai's allegiance, sounded him with an order from Dun.
proposals.reason: 不從 says Gan Zhuo did not follow Wang Dun, and 敦旨 is Wang Dun's order; the source does not call it forged.

proposals.before: Guo Mo was a man of Huai in Henan.
proposals.after: Guo Mo was a man of Huai in Henei.
proposals.reason: 河內 is Henei, not Henan.

proposals.before: Guo Mo came from Huai in Henan.
proposals.after: Guo Mo came from Huai in Henei.
proposals.reason: 河內 is Henei, not Henan.

proposals.before: He sent an envoy to visit Liu Kun; Kun added Mo as prefect of Henan.
proposals.after: He sent an envoy to visit Liu Kun; Kun appointed Mo prefect of Henei.
proposals.reason: 河內太守 is Prefect of Henei, not Henan.

proposals.before: He sent envoys to Liu Kun, who named him prefect of Henan.
proposals.after: He sent envoys to Liu Kun, who named him prefect of Henei.
proposals.reason: 河內太守 is Prefect of Henei, not Henan.

proposals.before: Mo was defeated in battle with Shi Cong; Ju turned ever weaker; Mo was deeply worried and afraid; he handed his seal to his adjutant Yin Yao, saying to him: "Prefect Li has treated me very generously; now I suddenly abandon him—I have no face to thank him; within three days you may report my departure."
proposals.after: Mo was defeated in battle with Shi Cong; Ju turned ever weaker; Mo was deeply worried and afraid; he handed his seal to his adjutant Yin Qiao, saying to him: "Prefect Li has treated me very generously; now I suddenly abandon him—I have no face to thank him; within three days you may report my departure."
proposals.reason: 殷嶠 is Yin Qiao (嶠, qiao), not Yin Yao.

proposals.before: Beaten by Shi Cong while Li Ju weakened, Guo Mo panicked, handed his seal to Yin Yao, and said, "Li Ju has been generous; I cannot face him if I slip away—announce my flight in three days."
proposals.after: Beaten by Shi Cong while Li Ju weakened, Guo Mo panicked, handed his seal to Yin Qiao, and said, "Li Ju has been generous; I cannot face him if I slip away—announce my flight in three days."
proposals.reason: 殷嶠 is Yin Qiao (嶠, qiao), not Yin Yao.

proposals.before: Su Jun sent Han Mian and others to attack Mo very urgently; inside the fort they were quite short of water; Mo feared, divided men and horses to go outside, then secretly slipped out from the south gate in a dash, leaving men to hold fast on defense.
proposals.after: Su Jun sent Han Chao and others to attack Mo very urgently; inside the fort they were quite short of water; Mo feared, divided men and horses to go outside, then secretly slipped out from the south gate in a dash, leaving men to hold fast on defense.
proposals.reason: 韓晁 is Han Chao (晁, chao), not Han Mian.

proposals.before: Su Jun sent Han Mian to hammer the fort; water ran low and Guo Mo panicked—he slipped part of his force outside, then broke out the south gate under cover while leaving a rear guard.
proposals.after: Su Jun sent Han Chao to hammer the fort; water ran low and Guo Mo panicked—he slipped part of his force outside, then broke out the south gate under cover while leaving a rear guard.
proposals.reason: 韓晁 is Han Chao (晁, chao), not Han Mian.

proposals.before: Minister of education Wang Dao, fearing he could not be controlled, thereupon greatly pardoned the realm, displayed Yin's head on the Great Pontoon bridge, and appointed Mo west camp general of the guard and inspector of Yu province.
proposals.after: Minister over the Masses Wang Dao, fearing he could not be controlled, thereupon proclaimed a general amnesty, displayed Yin's head on the Great Pontoon Bridge, and appointed Mo west camp general of the guard and inspector of Yu province.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not minister of education.

proposals.before: Wang Dao, fearing he could not contain him, proclaimed a general amnesty, spiked Liu Yin's head on the Great Floating Bridge, and named Guo Mo west camp general of the guard and inspector of Yu province.
proposals.after: Minister over the Masses Wang Dao, fearing he could not contain him, proclaimed a general amnesty, spiked Liu Yin's head on the Great Floating Bridge, and named Guo Mo west camp general of the guard and inspector of Yu province.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic field omits Wang Dao's explicit identifying office 司徒; the parallel literal field must also use the correct title.

proposals.before: Yet Ju was able with few to strike many, in battle victorious and captures many, thereby causing Xuanyuan to rage with resentment and Shilong to suffer setback.
proposals.after: Yet Ju was able with few to strike many, winning battles and taking many captives, thereby causing Liu Cong, Xuanming, to rage with resentment and Shi Le, Shilong, to suffer defeat.
proposals.reason: 玄明 is Liu Cong's courtesy name Xuanming, not “Xuanyuan”; 世龍 is Shi Le's courtesy name Shilong.

proposals.before: Li Ju in particular beat larger hosts again and again, stinging Liu Yao into fury and bruising Shi Hu.
proposals.after: Li Ju in particular beat larger hosts again and again, stinging Liu Cong into fury and bruising Shi Le.
proposals.reason: 玄明 identifies Liu Cong, not Liu Yao; 世龍 identifies Shi Le, not Shi Hu. The extraction itself correctly records these courtesy-name identifications.

proposals.before: Duan Pidi died at Shi Hu's hands for the same reason—the expectations of the crowd. How swiftly blessing turns to bane!
proposals.after: Duan Pidi died at Shi Le's hands for the same reason—the expectations of the crowd. How swiftly blessing turns to bane!
proposals.reason: 世龍 is Shi Le's courtesy name, not Shi Hu's.

decisions.reason: The Chinese personal name is 文鴦; 鴦 is read yang, so Wenyang is the correct English and pinyin form, not Wenying.
